c.tagline: A palm-fringed diving gateway on one of Africa's largest natural bays.

taxi.fareNote: There are no ride-hail apps in Pemba — agree the fare with the driver before setting off. Shared chapas (minibuses) are the cheapest way around, with taxis and tuk-tuks for short hops.

emergency.note: 112 works from mobile phones and connects to emergency services; landline numbers are 119 (police), 117 (ambulance) and 198 (fire).

avoid.reason: Cabo Delgado province — insurgency in the north; check advisories, avoid northern districts

hood_desc: The palm-lined main beach strip on the bay's ocean side, home to most of the resorts, dive centres, beach bars and seafood restaurants; the base most visitors choose for sun, snorkelling and diving.
The commercial and administrative heart of Pemba around Avenida 25 de Setembro and the market, with banks, shops, government offices and the airport road; the practical town centre.
The old lower town beside the harbour on the bay, with the port, dhow anchorage, fish market and faded Portuguese-era buildings; the working, historic waterfront of the city.

The dense, lively neighbourhood behind the town centre where much of Pemba's population lives, with busy street markets, chapa ranks and local eateries; an authentic, budget-friendly slice of the city.
The high ground overlooking Pemba Bay with villas, guesthouses and viewpoints across one of Africa's largest natural bays; a quieter residential base with sea views a little above the beach.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only.

transit.hours: Chapas run from around dawn until early evening; after dark, taxis and tuk-tuks are the main way to get around.
transit.note: Pemba has no formal public transport system; getting around means shared chapas (converted minibuses) along the main roads, plus taxis and tuk-tuks for door-to-door and beach runs.
transit.pay: Pay the chapa conductor in cash (roughly 15-25 meticais a hop); taxi and tuk-tuk fares are negotiated and paid in cash. Carry small notes.

ferry: Local dhows and boats across Pemba Bay

transit.m: Taxi to Wimbe Beach / town centre (10-15 min)
Chapa (shared minibus) toward the town centre

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~10% at tourist restaurants and for dive/tour guides is appreciated where service isn't already added.
